title: XY placenta -> maternal physiology -> human milk -> SCOBY/BC: full Janus reverse and placental-matrix branch

recent_anchor.study: High-throughput mRNA sequencing of human placenta shows sex differences across gestation
recent_anchor.finding: 124 first-trimester and 43 third-trimester placentas showed sex-dimorphic gene expression; sex chromosomes contributed a large fraction of the DEGs, with stronger dimorphism in first trimester.

epigenomic_anchor.study: Sex-differentiated placental methylation and gene expression regulation has implications for neonatal traits and adult diseases
epigenomic_anchor.finding: Placental autosomal methylation and its genetic regulation are extensively affected by fetal sex.

ecm_sex_signal_anchor.study: Examining Sex Differences in the Human Placental Transcriptome During the First Fetal Androgen Peak
ecm_sex_signal_anchor.finding: Female chorionic villi showed selective upregulation of extracellular-matrix components, while male-biased transcripts emphasized mitochondrial, immune and pregnancy-maintenance pathways.

scoBy_term_correction.importance: Observed fungal/yeast growth, bacterial-cellulose growth and mixed biomass must be distinguished experimentally.

milk_environment_prediction.BC_relevance: Komagataeibacter rhaeticus can produce bacterial cellulose on lactose/whey, but performance is strain-dependent and lower than on standard glucose medium in a published whey study.
milk_environment_prediction.yeast_relevance: Kombucha consortia can adapt to whey; yeast-community composition can shift strongly when lactose-utilizing taxa are favored.

conceptual_prediction: mammalian placental cells are unlikely to remain physiologically intact during an acidifying mixed fermentation
soluble proteins lipids metabolites nucleic acids and tissue-derived components may enter the surrounding liquid
collagen-rich insoluble ECM may persist longer than living cells and can serve as a physical surface/scaffold
yeasts and bacteria may colonize tissue surfaces or surrounding liquid depending on substrate access
BC may coat or interpenetrate accessible fibrous surfaces if the cellulose producer remains active and oxygen is available
proteolysis tissue breakdown or non-target microbial growth can dominate and make material attribution impossible
placental ECM provides collagen fibronectin laminin and GAG-rich fibrous architecture
BC can plausibly deposit around and interlock with an ECM scaffold
collagen can alter BC morphology mechanics and hydration behavior
sex-associated ECM differences may survive only if they are encoded in retained matrix composition or post-translational state; most cellular Y DNA should be removed by effective decellularization
mechanical benefit cannot be inferred without matched BC-only and ECM-only controls

direct_materials_anchor.study: An asymmetric bacterial cellulose/collagen membrane constructed via biological suturing and in situ pore formation
direct_materials_anchor.finding: Collagen introduced during Komagataeibacter fermentation became interwoven with growing BC, described by the authors as biological suturing.

y_chromosome_material_fate.raw_XY_placenta: XY fetal placental cells contain Y-chromosome DNA.
y_chromosome_material_fate.during_nonphysiological_mixed_culture: Human cells and DNA would be expected to lose viability/integrity over time; free DNA may persist transiently or adsorb to surfaces but this is not inheritance by the SCOBY.
y_chromosome_material_fate.BC_matrix_entrapment_claim: Physical entrapment of human DNA/proteins in a forming matrix is chemically conceivable but must be directly measured and is not equivalent to genetic incorporation.
y_chromosome_material_fate.decellularized_ECM: A properly decellularized matrix is specifically intended to remove cells, cell debris and much of the genetic material, reducing relevance of XY DNA while preserving structural ECM.

reverse_chain: a reproducible material effect requires a measurable phenotype such as BC yield morphology chemistry or mechanics
the phenotype must differ from milk-only BC-only placenta-only and process controls
a placenta-specific effect requires retained placental material to be identified in or on the BC matrix
a sex-specific placenta effect requires XY and XX placental material to differ after controlling gestational age pathology collection and processing
if decellularized ECM is used the relevant difference must survive decellularization as an ECM-level property
if raw tissue is used cellular debris blood and contamination must not explain the phenotype
a milk-sex effect requires direct compositional measurements rather than infant-sex label alone
a SCOBY effect requires distinguishing yeast biomass AAB activity and true bacterial cellulose
true BC formation requires compatible carbon metabolism and oxygen access
a Y-chromosome mechanism requires direct Y-DNA or Y-positive-cell detection and causal linkage; male-birth history alone is insufficient

preferred_non_operational_comparison_log: all claims remain observation-level until replicated
